title: fix(app-shell): give a flat view overlay's top-level columns a read path (objectui#8411)
body:
Fixes #8411

A flat view overlay's author-written top-level `columns` were being discarded on the read side, silently, while its tab kept rendering.

## The three reproduction readings — run on this repo's `main`, before any line changed

The card's evidence was explicitly *read, never executed*, and read against a pinned older sha (`7258eafbe614`) from the cloud repo. Triage and the PM both promoted reproduction to a blocking gate. All three readings were taken on `b89583ba9` with the source unmodified, by driving the real chain (`mergeViewsIntoObjects` -> `buildViewTabs`):

| # | reading | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | flat body (`viewKind` + `object` + top-level `columns`, no `config`) — does the tab render? | **YES** — `tab ids = crm_lead.compact`, label `Compact` |
| 2 | same reading — are the columns dropped? | **YES** — `tabs[0].columns = undefined` |
| 3 | positive control: an independent ViewItem with nested `config` | **columns render** — `[{"field":"name"},{"field":"owner"}]` |

Reading 1's raw entry, verbatim: `{"crm_lead.compact":{"name":"crm_lead.compact","label":"Compact","isDefault":false}}` — the collapse to `{ name, label, isDefault }` the card predicted, confirmed by execution rather than by reading.

Reading 3 is what makes readings 1 and 2 mean anything: without it, "the columns are lost" and "this harness never renders columns at all" are indistinguishable.

**The mechanism still holds on current `main`.** One measured detail beyond the card: it is not only `columns` that is lost — the flat body's entire inline body goes, `type` and `data` included (`buildViewTabs` then defaults `type` back to `grid`, which is part of why the screen looks correct).

Both fixtures were also parsed against the real `ViewMetadataSchema` (`@objectstack/spec` 17.3.0) and **both are accepted** — the flat overlay is a legitimate persisted shape, not off-spec metadata, so this is not a case for the contract-first "fix the producer" rule.

## The census, and which mechanism it selected

Searched with literal directories (wildcards do not prefix-match in a git pathspec) and with a lit control on every command shape — `git grep -n isViewItem` returns the known site at `MetadataProvider.tsx:347`, so the pathspec really searched.

**The literal conjunction `viewKind && object` exists in exactly one place.** But the *rule* — "is this row a standalone ViewItem record, or a flat body?" — is answered independently on **five** read-side sites:

| # | site | how it decides | the flat body's fate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `packages/app-shell/src/providers/MetadataProvider.tsx:348` `isViewItem` | `!!viewKind && !!object` | **body dropped** — this bug |
| 2 | `packages/app-shell/.../view-item-normalize.ts:60` `viewDisplayType` | `config.type` first, top-level `type` second | body read |
| 3 | `packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts:5046` `listViews` map | `spec.config` is an object | row returned verbatim |
| 4 | `packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts:2403` `isLegacyOverlayRow` | nested `config` ⇒ never an overlay row | classification only |
| 5 | `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx:1212` `resolveInternalForm` | `config` object **and** (`'viewKind' in spec` or `'object' in spec`) | body read from top level |

**Four of the five lead with the nested `config`** — spec's own discriminant — and every one of those four gives the flat body a path. `MetadataProvider.isViewItem` is the sole outlier and the sole site that loses author data. Site 3 even carries a comment saying it mirrors `mergeViewsIntoObjects` "so the two paths don't drift"; they had drifted, and this PR makes that comment true again.

⇒ The census selects **(a)** — align with spec's union and give the flat body an explicit path. What the measurement then added, and what reshaped how (a) had to land:

`mergeViewsIntoObjects` was conflating **two** questions that the other four sites keep apart:

- **Q1, binding** — does this row belong in an object's bucket? Answered `viewKind && object`.
- **Q2, body location** — is the body nested under `config` or inline? *Never asked* — the branch simply read `view.config` with a `{}` fallback.

Q1's predicate is **not** the part out of alignment, and that is measured, not assumed. Parsed against `ViewMetadataSchema`:

- a body with a nested `config` but **no `viewKind`** is **REJECTED** (`"No matching discriminator", discriminator: "viewKind"`);
- a flat body with **no `object`** is **REJECTED**;
- both ViewItem-family spellings (nested and flat) are **ACCEPTED**, and both carry both keys.

So every ViewItem-family member spec admits satisfies `viewKind && object`, and nothing spec admits is excluded by it. Narrowing Q1 to require `config` would push the flat overlay onto the container gate, whose key derivation (`view?.name || view?.list?.data?.object`) would bucket it under `crm_lead.compact` instead of `crm_lead` — turning "columns lost" into "tab lost too", the worse regression ruling ① forbids.

**So the fix lands entirely on Q2**, which is where spec's discriminant actually speaks. ①/② consistency: the flat body **stays on the ViewItem branch** (reading 1 preserved by construction), and that branch now reads its top-level body (reading 2 fixed).

### What this PR did NOT do, and why

Ruling ② also says to "collapse the predicate into ONE shared definition". That is **not deliverable inside this card's own fences** and was refused rather than half-done: sites 3-5 live in `@object-ui/data-objectstack` and `apps/console`, so a literal shared symbol needs a **new cross-package export** — the exact widening the acceptance rules out ("无新导出、无新 prop") — and `data-objectstack` importing from `app-shell` inverts the layering (app-shell depends on the adapter, not the reverse). The three also answer adjacent questions with their own local concerns (overlay-vs-saved classification, form-vs-list rejection), and all four are already correct. What this PR does collapse is the part it owns: the read side now asks spec's discriminant, in one named place, and stops being the outlier — the distinct read-side spellings go from five to four, with the only *wrong* one removed.

## The change

`packages/app-shell/src/providers/MetadataProvider.tsx` — the body resolution becomes an explicit, named, documented question:

- new `viewItemBody(view)` — a nested `config` is unwrapped as before; a body without one **is** the body, per spec's table ("an inline view config; no `config`, no container slot"). This replaces the `{}` fallback.
- `isViewItem` keeps its predicate and gains a docblock stating that it answers **binding only**, plus the parse readings that show why neither key can be dropped.

Not stripping the envelope keys off a flat body is deliberate and matches the sibling reader: `listViews` in `@object-ui/data-objectstack` returns a flat row verbatim, `object` and `viewKind` included, and `buildPersistedViewBody` treats a tab's `viewKind` as identity to relay — the same line `VIEW_OVERLAY_IDENTITY_KEYS` draws.

## ③ — the `isViewItemDraft` comment

Code untouched, exactly as ruled: whether the write-side predicate should align is objectui#3312, not this card. The two sentences claiming its `'viewKind' in value` test "is the same test `MetadataProvider.isViewItem()` applies on the read side" are factually wrong and would have become *more* wrong beside a changed read side, so they are replaced with what was measured — the three tests side by side (`'viewKind' in value` / `viewKind && object` / nested `config`), the observation that this one is the widest of the three (it admits a draft with `viewKind` and no `object`, which the read side does not), and an explicit routing of the difference to #3312. The one claim that *is* local and true — that both gates in that file read the one function, so they cannot drift from each other — is kept. No new confident assertion was substituted.

## Pin and reverse verification

`packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.flatOverlayColumns-8411.test.ts` pins the rendered outcome across the real chain (`ViewMetadataSchema` -> `mergeViewsIntoObjects` -> `buildViewTabs`), asserting both spellings **in one merge** with distinct columns each — so an implementation that collapsed the two shapes into one cannot pass, and the nested-`config` positive control is a standing assertion rather than a one-off reading.

Reverse verification, direction predicted before running and observed:

```
MUTATION anchors: removed=0 (want 0) injected=1 (want 1)
MUTATION blob: 5446dffd223ecfc75ee5a1b59f4dfab2bf3cf6ae (HEAD was 500f0996e9cfef14a8f75b7f1c4ba88a68486bbd)

 × renders a tab for the flat overlay AND carries its authored columns
 × keeps the two spellings distinct in one merge
AssertionError: expected undefined to deeply equal [ { field: 'name' }, ...(1) ]
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed | 2 passed (4)
```

The mutation was proven on disk before any result was read — anchor counts moved 1->0 and 0->1, and the blob hash changed — because an edit tool's exit code is not evidence a replacement matched. The **positive control stayed green** under the mutation, which is the point: the fix gives the flat body a path, it does not move the nested one. Restore verified byte-identical: disk blob back to `500f0996e9cfef14a8f75b7f1c4ba88a68486bbd`, `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status --porcelain` empty. The mutation ran under a `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` restoring by absolute path from `HEAD` (never a bare `git checkout --`, which would have restored the mutation itself out of the index).

## Gates

| gate | verdict line (the gate's own) |
|---|---|
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell test` | `Test Files  666 passed (666)` · `Tests  6429 passed | 1 skipped (6430)` — exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell lint` | `✖ 2948 problems (0 errors, 2948 warnings)` — exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell build` | `✓ dist completeness: 1 package(s) complete (922 emitted files verified)` — exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` | `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` — no diagnostics, exit 0 (the second project is what type-checks the test files, so the pin is covered) |
| pin, isolated | `Test Files  1 passed (1)` · `Tests  4 passed (4)` — exit 0 |
| `check-governed-queue-guard --test` (4 changed paths) | `✅ NOT GOVERNED — 4 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched.` — exit 0 |
| same command shape, `AGENTS.md` as **lit control** | `⛔ GOVERNED — 1 of 1 path(s) are on a governed surface` — exit 3 |

The lit control is what makes the `NOT GOVERNED` reading a measurement rather than a script that answers "no" to everything.

Heavy runs went through the container-wide verify lock (`OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT=issue-8411`); parallel agents were holding it, and the slot kept the queue place across waits.

## 验收备注

Observations found in passing, none filed and none fixed here — each with the successor that would carry it:

- **The read side answers "what is a ViewItem" in five places across three packages** (table above), and four of them are correct. This PR removes the wrong one but does not unify them; a literal shared definition needs a new cross-package export, which this card's acceptance forbids. *Successor: objectui#3312*, which already owns "which of the two shapes should be the single authorable shape" — the unification question is downstream of that answer.
- **`data-objectstack`'s `listViews` and `mergeViewsIntoObjects` still stamp differently for a flat row** — the adapter returns the row verbatim, the provider additionally stamps `name`/`label`/`isDefault`. Bodies now agree (which is what the adapter's "so the two paths don't drift" comment claims); the envelope stamping was never claimed to match. *Successor: none — no PR or reader is blocked by it, recorded only so a future reader of that comment knows exactly how far the mirroring goes.*
- **A flat *form*-family overlay** (`viewKind: 'form'` with `sections` at top level) was **rejected** by `ViewMetadataSchema` in a side probe, while the flat *list* overlay was accepted. The fix is family-agnostic (`applyViewItem` routes `form` into `formViews` either way), so nothing here depends on the answer, and the probe was one fixture — not enough to call it a defect. *Successor: none — not filed, because a single rejected fixture of my own construction is as likely to be my fixture's shape as the schema's boundary; it would need its own measurement before it is a claim.*

## 维护者速读(草稿)

**改了什么。** 一个「扁平」写法的视图 body(`viewKind` + `object`,列直接写在顶层,没有嵌套的 `config`)在读取时,作者写的 `columns` 会被静默丢掉。改动只有一处实质逻辑:读取侧现在先问「body 在哪里」——有嵌套 `config` 就取 `config`(和以前一样),没有就把这一行本身当作 body(以前这里是空对象 `{}`)。另外按裁决改了 `clientValidation.ts` 里两句写错的注释(只改注释,不动代码)。

**为什么改。** `@objectstack/spec` 明确把这种扁平写法列为**合法的持久化形状**之一(已实测:schema 确实接受它),所以问题不在写的人、也不在 spec,而在本仓读取侧欠它一条路径。最糟的是它**不报错**:tab 照常显示,界面看上去完全正常,作者只会以为「我列写错了」,而实际上他的列从来没被读过。仓内另外四个读取点早就是按 `config` 来判断的,只有这一处没有,本次把它对齐。

**风险与代价(含回滚)。** 风险低。判断「这一行属于哪个对象」的逻辑一个字没动,所以**不会多出或少掉任何一个 tab**;唯一的行为变化是:以前被丢掉的字段现在会带上。整包 666 个测试文件、6429 个测试全绿,lint 0 error。回滚代价极小:把 `viewItemBody` 里的 `: view` 改回 `: {}` 即可完全恢复旧行为(反向核验已经实跑过这条路径,pin 会立刻变红)。需要留意的一点:扁平 body 现在会把 `object` / `viewKind` 一并带到 tab 上——这是**刻意**的,与 `@object-ui/data-objectstack` 读同一行时的行为一致(它直接原样返回整行)。

**席位意见。** *(留空,待 PM 席位填写)*

**你要做的。** 正常评审即可,不涉及受管面(门禁已确认,并用 `AGENTS.md` 做了阳性对照)。若你认为跨包的「同一规则五处实现」应当在本卡内一并收口,请驳回本 PR 的这一取舍——上面「验收备注」第一条写明了为什么本卡没有做,以及它为什么被挂到 objectui#3312。
